combos.why: The paint version of the same idea. Pattern scale is a separate control.
Independent spec must be ticked first.

faq.q: Why is my texture huge?
faq.a: Scale 1.00 on a whole-car canvas is often too big. Go to 0.3 to 0.6.

faq.q: Does spec scale change the paint?
faq.a: No. Spec only.

faq.q: What is the best size?
faq.a: Features of 8 to 32 pixels at 2048.

faq.q: Does rotation work on flat finishes?
faq.a: There is nothing to turn on a flat spec. It needs a texture, such as brushed grain or a weave.

mistakes.symptom: Scale is greyed out.
mistakes.cause: INDEPENDENT SPEC is not ticked.
mistakes.fix: Tick it first.

mistakes.symptom: Fine detail disappears in the preview.
mistakes.cause: The preview is smaller than the 2048 export.
mistakes.fix: Zoom in or read the spec views before deciding it did nothing.

protips: Preview is about 768 pixels for a 2048 sheet. Micro flake and holographic grating at small scale average out and look flat there.
Rotation of 45 degrees on a weave is the quickest way to a different carbon look.

articles.title: R, G and B channel sliders
articles.summary: The R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT sliders nudge the finish spec. They add or subtract under the zone and then the app clips to safe limits.
articles.what: These three sliders shift each channel by up to 127 either way, in steps of 5. The shift is added to the finish spec under the zone shape, then clipped at the floors: 0 for metal, 15 for roughness and 16 for coat. They are the fine-tuning tool after you pick a finish. The built-in Feels set them in one click.
when: A finish is almost right but a touch too dull or too rough
You want a consistent tweak across several zones
how: Open the zone editor, go to the BASE section and find Spec Sliders.
Move R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT.
Use the Feel picker or the save icon for presets.

controls.label: R METAL
controls.effect: Metal shift.

controls.label: G ROUGH
controls.effect: Roughness shift.

controls.label: B COAT
controls.effect: Coat shift, added to the coat value. Left is glossier, right is duller.

tips: For a wetter look, lower G ROUGH, and lower B COAT if the finish coat is above 16.
The B COAT slider tooltip in the app says higher is a stronger mirror. The number is really added to the coat value, where bigger means duller, so judge by eye in the preview.
pitfalls: Shifts that reach a floor stop having an effect.
Large shifts can cancel the finish character.

actions.label: Spec Sliders (R Metal, G Rough, B Coat)

deep.heading: Exactly what a slider does
deep.body: Each slider adds its value, from minus 127 to plus 127, to that channel under the zone mask. The result is clipped at 0 to 255, with floors of 0 for metal, 15 for roughness and 16 for coat. Sliders at 0 (or all under half a point) are ignored. The sliders run after patterns, overlays and blend modes, so they are the last creative step; only Remap, Override and Lighting Mask come after.

deep.heading: Which way each one goes
deep.body: Metal plus means more metal. Roughness plus means duller, minus means glossier. Coat plus means duller, because blue is backwards, minus means glossier and stops at 16. Rough recipes: satin from gloss is G ROUGH plus 40 to plus 80 with B COAT plus 30 to plus 60. Wetter is G ROUGH minus and B COAT minus.

deep.heading: Sliders versus other tools
deep.body: Sliders shift a whole zone evenly. Material Remap squeezes a channel into a new low to high range and keeps variation. Material Override sets flat values. Spec Strength pulls everything toward neutral. A shift of 20 is subtle, 50 is a clear style change, and anything near 100 usually cancels the finish character.

examples.title: Satin from gloss
examples.goal: Take a gloss body to satin without changing the base.
examples.result: Roughness around 90 and coat around 61: a quiet satin.

examples.title: Duller candy
examples.goal: Take some wet depth out of a candy zone.
examples.result: Roughness 45 and coat 36: the candy colour stays but the glassy look relaxes into a satin candy.

combos.why: Feels are slider combinations saved as one click.
The tools that run right after the sliders.
The floors that clip slider results.

faq.q: Why does B COAT plus make it duller?
faq.a: Because blue is backwards. The number is added to the coat value, where bigger means less coat.

faq.q: Why did my slider stop working?
faq.a: The channel reached its floor or ceiling.

faq.q: Can sliders recolour?
faq.a: No. They only change metal, roughness and coat.

faq.q: Slider or SPEC STRENGTH?
faq.a: Use the slider to move one channel. Use strength to scale the whole finish.

mistakes.symptom: Large shifts make the finish look generic.
mistakes.cause: A shift near 100 overwhelms the base values.
mistakes.fix: Choose a different base finish and nudge by 20 to 40.

mistakes.symptom: Wetter did not work on a gel coat.
mistakes.cause: It is already at the floor of 15 and 16.
mistakes.fix: Nothing more to gain. Change the pattern or the paint.

protips: The B COAT slider tooltip in the app says higher is a stronger mirror. The number is really added to the coat value where bigger means duller, so judge by eye.
Save a good slider set as a Feel so it can be reused on other zones.

articles.title: Material override, remap and lighting mask
articles.summary: MASK > Advanced spec utilities has power tools: copy a material onto a zone, squeeze a channel into a new range, and set how much lighting each area gets.
articles.what: Material Sampler lets you sample a spot on an existing spec and apply that material to a zone. Material Range Remapper re-maps each channel into a low and high range. A source value of 0 goes to Low and 255 goes to High, so you can calm or intensify a whole spec. Lighting Mask sets alpha: use the source, full lighting, reduced lighting or kill lighting. A Decal Rescue Kit also fixes decals that came in shiny.
when: You like the shine of one part of a spec and want it elsewhere
You need a quick overall change to an imported spec
Decals look glassy and need to go flat
how: Open the MASK menu in the top bar, then Advanced spec utilities.
Choose Material Range Remapper, set Low and High for M, R and CC, then apply. Restore Original puts it back.
Choose Lighting Mask and pick a mode.
Choose Decal Rescue Kit for Flat Vinyl and similar fixes.

controls.label: Remap Low and High
controls.effect: Squeezes a channel into a new range.

tips: Remap presets: Original, Metallic Texture, Printed Vinyl, Matte Texture, Gloss Texture.
pitfalls: Remapping can push the coat into the forbidden 1 to 15 band; the app raises it back to 16.

deep.heading: The order the three tools run
deep.body: After the sliders, the zone spec goes through Material Remap first, then Material Override, then Lighting Mask. All three run before the final floors, so a flat override of roughness 5 on a non-chrome pixel is lifted to 15 and a coat of 1 to 15 is lifted to 16. Remap and Override work per channel (metal, roughness, coat); Lighting Mask only touches alpha.

deep.heading: Remap in numbers
deep.body: Remap squeezes a channel into a new low and high range: result = low + source / 255 times (high minus low). A source 0 goes to Low and a source 255 goes to High. A metal range of 0 to 100 turns a chrome (255) into metal 100 but keeps every bit of variation, so a brushed grain stays brushed while the whole thing calms down. Override is blunt: it sets one flat value for the channel across the zone and loses all variation.

deep.heading: Sampler and decal rescue
deep.body: The Material Sampler reads the exact metal, roughness and coat at a spot (Point, 3 by 3 median or 5 by 5 median) and can copy them onto the active zone. Decal Rescue Kit puts a plain non-metal spec under stamped numbers and sponsors: Flat Vinyl, Satin Decal or Gloss Decal, so they do not take the sparkle of whatever spec is below.

examples.title: Calm a too-sparkly metallic
examples.goal: Keep the texture, lower the metal.
examples.result: The brightest flakes now peak at metal 120 and every pattern shape is still there.

examples.title: Rescue sponsor logos
examples.goal: Stop numbers and sponsors from going sparkly under chrome.

settings.Body zone: Limited to the car paint layer

examples.result: Decals keep a plain non-metal look while the body stays chrome.

combos.why: Sliders run just before these tools, so a remap or override can overrule a slider.
Lighting Mask is the tool that changes alpha.
The floors run after all three tools.

faq.q: Remap or slider?
faq.a: Sliders move the whole zone evenly. Remap rescales the range and keeps the variation.

faq.q: Can I undo a remap?
faq.a: Yes. Restore Original puts the zone back.

faq.q: What does Override do to texture?
faq.a: It flattens the channel to one value, so texture in that channel is lost.

faq.q: Do these tools change colour?
faq.a: No. They only change spec channels and alpha.

mistakes.symptom: My override of coat 5 became 16.
mistakes.cause: The floors run after the tools.
mistakes.fix: Use 16 or more.

mistakes.symptom: Override removed my brushed grain.
mistakes.cause: A flat value replaces the channel.
mistakes.fix: Use Remap, which keeps variation.

mistakes.symptom: Numbers look sparkly or dull.
mistakes.cause: Stamped items take the spec of whatever is under them.
mistakes.fix: Use Decal Rescue Kit and limit the body zone to the car paint layer.

protips: Remap presets are a fast start: Original, Metallic Texture, Printed Vinyl, Matte Texture and Gloss Texture. Then fine tune Low and High.
Use the Material Sampler first. Copying exact numbers from a part you like is quicker than guessing.

articles.title: Spec blend modes
articles.summary: SPEC BLEND decides how a spec overlay mixes with the base spec. The named modes, Ghost Carve and friends, are made for racing finishes.
articles.what: The dropdown offers Normal, Ghost Carve, Chrome Inlay, Frost Etch, Angle Flip, Ember Gate and Depth Press, plus the classic Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Hard Light and Soft Light. Each named mode has a one-line help text in the dropdown. Use Normal while learning. Try Chrome Inlay when you want an overlay to cut a mirror shape into the surface.
when: An overlay hides the base spec instead of working with it
You want the texture to cut in, glow or flip at angles
how: Open the zone and find SPEC BLEND.
Pick a mode and read its help line.
Render and judge at car scale.

controls.label: SPEC BLEND
controls.range: Normal, Ghost Carve, Chrome Inlay, Frost Etch, Angle Flip, Ember Gate, Depth Press, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Hard Light, Soft Light
controls.effect: Chooses how the overlay mixes with the base spec.

tips: Compare Normal and the named mode side by side before you commit.
pitfalls: A strong overlay with a classic blend can wash out a finish.

deep.heading: The six named modes rewrite three channels
deep.body: Ghost Carve pulls the coat value toward 64 plus 176 times the pattern, so pattern lows and highs land at very different coat values and form carved cells, and lowers roughness by up to 25. It leaves the metal alone, so any base keeps its tinted flash. Chrome Inlay lowers metal (by up to 85 percent) and roughness (by up to 65 percent) where the pattern is hot and pushes the coat value toward 245: a mirror inlay in a metal surround. Frost Etch lowers metal by up to 45, raises roughness by up to 150 and lowers the coat value by up to 35: sandblasted, milky areas. Angle Flip adds up to plus or minus 85 metal and moves the coat value by the opposite sign, up to 135, so the pattern shows at one angle and inverts at another. Ember Gate lights only the top ridges: above a pattern value of 0.80 the coat value goes to 252 and roughness to 34. Depth Press embosses: a lit rim (metal plus 110, coat plus 90) and a shadow rim (metal minus 70).

deep.heading: Without a pattern the zone itself is the field
deep.body: These modes work with or without a pattern. With a pattern the pattern drives the effect. Without one, the zone's own paint structure drives it, so your livery becomes the carve: the field is the paint brightness first, the base spec shape second, a flat 0.5 last. Flat solid zones with a featureless base respond only subtly, so give the mode some structure to work with.

deep.heading: The legacy five
deep.body: Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Hard Light and Soft Light are the older blend modes that mix the overlay values with the base. They keep working but can wash out a finish, and a strong overlay under a classic mode may flatten it. The named modes are physical: they change how metal, gloss and coat behave, not just brightness. All modes honour the iron floors afterward.

examples.title: Carve a livery into chrome
examples.goal: Make the livery shapes read as mirror cuts.
examples.result: Hot parts of the pattern become mirror-like inlays while the surround loses most of its metal.

examples.title: Colour-flip from any base
examples.goal: Get angle-dependent flashes on a dark colour.
examples.result: Cells with different coat values flash sky or sun colour as the car turns, while the metal stays tinted and dark.

combos.why: Ghost Carve is the recipe behind most angle-reveal finishes.
Blend decides how an overlay meets the base; the stack decides the order.
See where the blend sits in the order of operations.

faq.q: Which mode for sparkle that ignites on edges?
faq.a: Ember Gate. Only the brightest ridges light up.

faq.q: Which mode for a stamped look?
faq.a: Depth Press. Every element gets a lit rim and a shadow rim.

faq.q: Why does nothing change on my plain zone?
faq.a: Flat solid zones with featureless bases respond subtly. Add a pattern or a structured base.

faq.q: Do the modes change the colour?
faq.a: No. They change metal, roughness and coat only.

mistakes.symptom: The effect is too strong and everything is chrome.
mistakes.cause: Strength and pattern spec amount both high with Chrome Inlay.
mistakes.fix: Lower strength before the next layer.

mistakes.symptom: Ghost Carve shows nothing.
mistakes.cause: The base colour is too bright, so diffuse colour hides the flashes.
mistakes.fix: Crush the colour near black and judge on a daytime track.

mistakes.symptom: A classic blend washed out my finish.
mistakes.cause: Legacy modes mix values directly.
mistakes.fix: Switch to a named mode or lower strength.

protips: Compare Normal and the named mode side by side before you commit.
Angle Flip is the one to try for a finish that changes between camera angles in replays.

articles.title: Spec patterns and overlay stacks
articles.summary: Spec patterns add texture to the shine only. Stack up to five per zone and tune each one.
articles.what: A spec pattern is a texture for the spec map, such as brushed grain, carbon weave, hex cells or micro sparkle. It changes how light plays, never the colour. The catalogue has 301 of them in 34 groups. In a zone, expand the SPEC OVERLAYS section and click Add Spec Overlay. You can stack up to five. Each layer has move up and down, Duplicate, Mute, Solo and Inspect, plus its own Strength, M, R and C channel ticks, Size, Rotation, X and Y position, Blend and a Coverage box.
when: You want carbon, brushed or sparkle texture without touching the colour
You want a unique surface on one part of the car
how: Open the zone and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click Add Spec Overlay and pick a pattern.
Set Strength (default 50) and the channels M, R and C that it should touch.
Use Mute and Solo to compare layers.

controls.label: Add Spec Overlay
controls.effect: Adds a spec texture layer.

controls.label: SPEC OVERLAYS section
controls.effect: Per layer tuning.

tips: Solo one layer at a time when you debug a busy look.
Pick M, R or C on purpose: texture on roughness only is the safest.
pitfalls: Five layers at full strength fight each other.
Spec overlays change shine only. If you want visible shapes on the paint, use a pattern.

deep.heading: How an overlay changes the spec
deep.body: Each spec overlay moves the finished material toward its own target on the channels you tick (M, R, C): result = current + (target minus current) times coverage times strength. Strength defaults to 50 percent. Overlays are applied last on the finished material, so the base cannot undo them, and the later sliders and floors still apply afterward.

deep.heading: Order and channels
deep.body: The stack runs from the first layer to the fifth, each mixing onto the result of the one before. Texture on roughness only is the safest: it changes how light spreads without touching metal or the coat. M-only overlays add sparkle on metal. C-only overlays vary the clearcoat and tend to be the most visible in direct sun. Five layers at full strength fight each other, so build with two or three and balance their strengths.

deep.heading: Debugging a busy look
deep.body: Mute turns a layer off without deleting it and Solo shows only that layer. Inspect reads the numbers at a spot. Because spec overlays never change colour, a flat colour preview looks identical with and without them. Use the spec views (R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) or the Channels readout to confirm they did anything.

examples.title: Brushed steel hood
examples.goal: Real brushed texture on a metallic base.
examples.result: Fine directional grain with occasional bright glints.

examples.title: Carbon under gloss
examples.goal: Visible weave only in the shine.
examples.result: A weave that moves with the light while the paint stays a plain colour.

combos.why: The blend mode changes how each overlay meets the base spec.
Where to find each kind of overlay.
Paint patterns and spec overlays both stack to five, but only patterns change colour.

faq.q: How many overlays can I stack?
faq.a: Up to five per zone.

faq.q: Why does my overlay do nothing in the preview?
faq.a: Overlays change shine only. Check the spec views.

faq.q: What strength should I use?
faq.a: Start at 50, the default, and go lower if the look is loud. 30 to 50 reads as subtle flake.

faq.q: Can I mute a layer?
faq.a: Yes. Mute, Solo and Duplicate are on each layer.

mistakes.symptom: Everything looks noisy.
mistakes.cause: Several overlays at high strength on all three channels.
mistakes.fix: Solo each layer, tick fewer channels, lower strength.

mistakes.symptom: The old stack disappeared.
mistakes.cause: Setting overlays through an apply command replaces the stack.
mistakes.fix: Add layers one at a time with Add Spec Overlay.

protips: A subtle flake overlay at strength 30 to 50 adds depth to almost any finish.
Pick the channel on purpose. The same pattern on R, on M and on C gives three different looks.

articles.title: Spec presets and Feels
articles.summary: Feels are one-click spec tweaks. Wet Candy, Track Flash, Chrome Mirror, Deep Gloss, Soft Pearl and Satin Matte are built in.
articles.what: A Feel sets the three channel sliders at once. The built-in Feels are, as metal, rough and coat shifts: Wet Candy 30, -55, -45. Track Flash 55, -35, -60. Chrome Mirror 80, -80, -70. Deep Gloss 25, -45, -85. Soft Pearl 15, 25, 10. Satin Matte -25, 65, 40. The disk icon saves your own Feel on this computer.
when: You want a quick consistent shine change across zones
You found a combination you want to reuse
how: Open the zone editor, go to the BASE section and find Spec Sliders.
Pick a Feel from the preset list.
To keep your own, set the sliders and click the save icon.

controls.label: Spec preset
controls.effect: Applies metal, rough and coat shifts at once.

controls.label: Save preset
controls.effect: Saves your slider settings as a Feel.

tips: Apply a Feel, then fine tune by 5.
pitfalls: Feels stack on top of the finish, so a Feel on a matte finish will not make it chrome.
The coat part of a Feel follows the backwards coat scale: the four gloss Feels use minus numbers (glossier) and Soft Pearl and Satin Matte use plus numbers (duller). Judge the result by eye.

deep.heading: What each Feel really does
deep.body: A Feel is three slider values applied at once, each between minus 127 and plus 127. Wet Candy is metal plus 30, roughness minus 55, coat minus 45. Track Flash is 55, minus 35, minus 60. Chrome Mirror is 80, minus 80, minus 70. Deep Gloss is 25, minus 45, minus 85. Soft Pearl is 15, 25, 10. Satin Matte is minus 25, plus 65, plus 40. Roughness minus always means glossier. The coat byte is backwards, so a minus coat number makes the coat glossier (it stops at 16) and a plus number makes it duller. The four gloss Feels use minus coat numbers; Soft Pearl and Satin Matte use plus numbers to soften the coat.

deep.heading: Feels sit on top of the finish
deep.body: They are added to whatever the finish already is, then clipped at 0 for metal, 15 for roughness and 16 for coat. So Chrome Mirror on a matte finish will not make it chrome: metal 0 plus 80 and roughness 200 minus 80 is a satin metal. On a gloss finish the same Feel makes a real step toward chrome.

deep.heading: Your own Feels
deep.body: Set the three sliders, click the save icon, and the Feel is kept on this computer next to the built-in ones. They are not shared with other computers or other drivers.

examples.title: Candy glow
examples.goal: More wet depth on a coloured gloss.
examples.result: Roughness drops and metal rises a little for a deeper, glassier colour.

examples.title: Quick stealth
examples.goal: Turn a gloss zone into a flat one.
examples.result: Roughness 30 plus 65 is 95 and coat 16 plus 40 is 56: a satin from gloss in one click.

combos.why: A Feel is just three slider values; fine tune them by hand afterward.
Auto-Pop is the automatic version of a Feel.

faq.q: Do Feels change colour?
faq.a: No.

faq.q: Can I stack two Feels?
faq.a: A Feel sets the sliders, so a second one replaces the first.

faq.q: Where are saved Feels kept?
faq.a: On this computer only.

faq.q: Which Feel for chrome?
faq.a: Chrome Mirror, but start from a gloss or metallic base. On a matte base it will only reach satin metal.

mistakes.symptom: A Feel did nothing on chrome.
mistakes.cause: The finish was already at the limit of the channels the Feel pushes.
mistakes.fix: Pick a Feel that pushes the other way.

mistakes.symptom: The coat looks duller with Satin Matte.
mistakes.cause: Its coat number is plus 40 and the coat scale is backwards, so a plus number softens the coat on purpose.
mistakes.fix: That is the satin look. Lower B COAT by 5s if you want a wetter edge.

protips: Apply a Feel, then fine tune in steps of 5.
Feels are a good way to learn the sliders: apply one and look at what the R, G and B values became.

articles.title: Auto-Pop
articles.summary: Auto-Pop gives a zone a small, safe boost of shine in one click and can be undone in a single step.
articles.what: Auto-Pop looks at the zone average and nudges only what is weak. It adds up to 15 metal if the zone metal averages under 70. It lowers roughness by up to 45 if the roughness averages above 70. It lowers the coat value by up to 45 if the coat averages above 55, which makes it glossier. All steps are multiples of 5. If the zone is already glossy it says so and changes nothing.
when: A zone looks dull and you want a quick lift
You want a safe starting point before hand tuning
how: Open the zone editor, go to the BASE section and find Spec Sliders.
Click Auto-Pop.
Press Undo if you do not like it. It is a single step.

controls.label: Auto-Pop
controls.effect: Adds a small shine boost to weak channels.

tips: Repeat clicks keep boosting until the limits are reached.
pitfalls: It will not turn a matte finish into chrome.

deep.heading: The exact thresholds
deep.body: Auto-Pop reads the zone average from the spec preview. If the metal average is under 70 it adds up to 15 metal, 30 percent of the gap to 70. If roughness averages over 70 it lowers roughness by the excess, up to 45. If the coat averages over 55 it lowers the coat value by the excess, up to 45, which is glossier. Every step is a multiple of 5 and it only moves in the direction of gloss. A zone that is already glossy gets a note and no change.

deep.heading: What it needs and what it does not do
deep.body: It needs a spec preview to have been rendered first, because it measures the real zone spec. It adds to the three sliders, so it can be undone in one step. It will not turn matte into chrome, because the metal boost is capped at 15 and roughness and coat drop by at most 45 per click. Repeated clicks keep boosting until the limits are reached.

examples.title: Rescue a dull zone
examples.goal: Add life to a zone that renders flat.
examples.result: The sliders move by a few steps toward more metal and less roughness. Check the car and press Undo if it is not right.

examples.title: Already glossy
examples.goal: See that Auto-Pop respects a good zone.
examples.result: It says the zone is already glossy and changes nothing.

combos.why: Auto-Pop moves these three sliders.
For a bigger, deliberate move use a Feel.

faq.q: Will Auto-Pop wreck my finish?
faq.a: No. It is small, conservative, and one Undo step.

faq.q: Why does it ask me to render first?
faq.a: It measures the real spec preview of the zone.

faq.q: Does it add colour?
faq.a: No. Spec only.

faq.q: Can I use it twice?
faq.a: Yes, each click boosts again until the limits.

mistakes.symptom: Nothing happened.
mistakes.cause: The zone is already glossy, or no spec preview was rendered.
mistakes.fix: Render a preview first and read the message.

mistakes.symptom: I wanted a matte car shiny.
mistakes.cause: Auto-Pop is capped at gentle steps.
mistakes.fix: Use a Feel or choose a different base finish.

protips: Auto-Pop is a safe first move when a zone looks dull and you do not know why.
After Auto-Pop the sliders hold real numbers, so you can read them to learn what the zone needed.

articles.title: The Spec Map Inspector
articles.summary: The Inspector lets you look at the spec channels one at a time and read exact values from any spot.
articles.what: Open MASK > Advanced spec utilities and choose Material Sampler. The channel buttons ALL, R, G, B and A switch the view. The Sample area menu offers Point, 3 by 3 Median and 5 by 5 Median. A table shows the minimum, maximum and mean of each channel. Copy M, R, CC and A copy the sampled numbers. Select Connected and Select All Similar find matching areas, using a Material tolerance from 0 to 64 (default 12). Apply to Active Zone and Clear Zone Override finish the job.
when: You want to read exactly what a finish is doing
You want to copy a material from one place to another
how: Open MASK > Advanced spec utilities, then Material Sampler.
Pick a channel view and a sample size.
Click the car or the template to sample.
Use Select Connected or Select All Similar, then Apply to Active Zone.

controls.label: Material tolerance
controls.effect: How close a match must be.

controls.label: Sample size
controls.effect: Averages around the click.

tips: Use Median sampling on noisy textures.
pitfalls: Point sampling on grain gives a random value. Use the median.

deep.heading: Seeing the real numbers
deep.body: The Material Sampler shows exact metal, roughness, coat and alpha at a clicked spot. The channel buttons ALL, R, G, B and A switch the preview between the channels. The Sample area menu offers Point, 3 by 3 Median and 5 by 5 Median, and a table lists the minimum, maximum and mean of each channel. Use Median on any textured area, because a single point on grain gives a random value.

deep.heading: Finding and copying a material
deep.body: Select Connected grows from the clicked pixel across touching similar pixels; Select All Similar finds every matching pixel on the car. Material tolerance runs from 0 to 64 with a default of 12. Copy M, R, CC and A copy the numbers, and Apply to Active Zone writes them as an override for the zone. Clear Zone Override undoes it.

deep.heading: The material readout
deep.body: After a preview renders, the app also reports the material mix of the whole spec as a bar: percent glossy, metallic and matte, with plain warnings for flat or whitewashed settings, such as coat in the 1 to 15 dead band or a metal floor too low. Treat it as a quick check before you export.

examples.title: Copy the exact chrome from one part
examples.goal: Match the chrome on a bumper to the hood.

settings.Action: Copy M, R, CC, then Apply to Active Zone

examples.result: The hood zone gets the same metal, roughness and coat as the bumper.

examples.title: Verify a matte
examples.goal: Check a matte finish is truly matte.
examples.result: The roughness reads around 200 or more and the readout shows mostly matte.

combos.why: Colour tells you the family; the Sampler tells you the number.
Apply to Active Zone is an override.

faq.q: Why does the same finish read different values?
faq.a: Textured finishes vary. Use Median sampling and compare means.

faq.q: Is the Sampler changing my car?
faq.a: Not until you press Apply to Active Zone.

faq.q: What tolerance should I use?
faq.a: 12 is the default. Raise it to find broader areas.

faq.q: Does it show the preview or the export?
faq.a: The preview spec. The export runs the same steps at full size.

mistakes.symptom: Values jump between clicks.
mistakes.cause: Point sampling on a textured area.
mistakes.fix: Switch to a Median size.

mistakes.symptom: Select All Similar grabbed too much.
mistakes.cause: Tolerance too high.
mistakes.fix: Lower it toward 12 or less.

protips: Sample the spot you like, copy the numbers, then recreate it with a base and sliders. You learn what makes it.
Bright green in the spec colour views means rough, not shiny.

articles.title: Colour shift and angle reveal
articles.summary: iRacing cannot truly change hue with the viewing angle, so colour shift looks are built by hiding colour in dark paint and revealing it with fine spec detail.
articles.what: A true colour-flip paint is not possible with the sim shader. The trick is to bury the colours in a near-black base and add fine spec pins, 8 to 32 pixels wide, that catch the light at certain angles. As the car turns, those pins flash and the colour appears to move. Foundation EFX, Prizm, Spectrum Shift and the Fractured shelves use this idea. It needs very fine detail to work, and it needs a deep, dark base.

Keep the base dark.
Do not scale the pattern up. Fine detail is the point.

deep.heading: The mechanism in three lobes
deep.body: There is no true colour rotation in the sim. What exists is paint-tinted metal, environment-coloured clear coat and roughness gating. Metal at 176 to 255 keeps the reflection tinted with the paint hue even when the paint is nearly black. The clear coat is a separate, nearly white lobe that mirrors the environment: teal sky at one angle, gold sun or tarmac at another. Crushing the base colour removes the diffuse light, so only the two lobes remain and cells flip between dark and flash as the car turns.

deep.heading: What it needs to read
deep.body: Two cell styles work: large coherent cells (the Ghost Shift recipe) and fine cells of 8 to 32 pixels whose channels disagree (the Fractured and ColorShoxx style). For the fine style use 6 to 8 crushed near-black shades (about 10 to 18 percent lightness) so metal cells cross lighting thresholds at different times. A single flat magenta carrier looks dead. Two routes work: a dark buried palette (any hue, best for warm, green and copper) or a bright cool base (blue, violet, magenta). Warm bright bases blend into warm sun and lose the second colour.

deep.heading: Where to judge it
deep.body: Flash colours come from the track's sky and sun, so daytime tracks show them best and night or indoor lighting mutes them. Judge on the curved hood, roof and fenders, because a flat door can hold the base look longer. A good one reveals panel by panel, not the whole car at once, and survives shade, glare and replay distance.

faq.q: Can paint really change colour with the angle?
faq.a: Not with a true shader. Colour-shift finishes fake it with paint plus spec.

faq.q: Why does the effect disappear at night?
faq.a: The flash colours come from the sky and sun; night mutes them.

faq.q: Why dark colours?
faq.a: A bright paint adds diffuse light that hides the two specular lobes.

faq.q: Does the preview show it?
faq.a: The flat preview cannot show angle changes. Judge it in the sim on a daytime track.

mistakes.symptom: It reads as sparkle, not a shift.
mistakes.cause: Pins or cells too large or all one shade.
mistakes.fix: Use finer cells and 6 to 8 dark shades.

mistakes.symptom: The second colour never shows.
mistakes.cause: A warm bright base blended into warm sun.
mistakes.fix: Use a dark buried palette, or a cool bright base.

mistakes.symptom: Hot pink spec did not flip.
mistakes.cause: Pink is only how the bytes pack. The effect needs spatial pattern, dark paint and lighting.
mistakes.fix: Add the pattern and crush the paint.

protips: Offset the clear-coat structure from the metal structure so the two lobes peak at different angles.
Judge on a daytime track and on the hood and fenders, not on a flat door.

articles.title: The spec pattern groups
articles.summary: The 301 spec patterns are sorted into groups such as sparkle, brushed metal, carbon weave, clearcoat, weather and wear, and animal skins.
articles.what: The original 181 sit in 25 groups: Sparkle and Micro-Metal 8, Optical and Interference 7, Directional Metal and Brush 4, Carbon and Composite Weave 9, Clearcoat and Coating 4, Structure and Geometry 10, Surface and Spray Texture 4, Organic and Natural 4, Weather, Wear and Track 6, Racing and Livery Story 3, Mechanical and Industrial 1, Exotic and Kinetic 3, Precision and Guilloche 6, Artistic and Abstract 1, Predator Skins 8, Dangerous Animals 10, Gothic and Horror 4, Voodoo Inspired 10, Rising Sun Spec 9, Engine-Turn and Machined 1, Fire and Heat 1, Holographic and Color-Shift 1, Source Pattern Plates 24, Definitive Spec Replacements 33 and Let Freedom Ring 10. A newer set of 120 overlays adds more machined, crystal and surface textures. Every spec pattern changes the shine only.

deep.heading: How the 301 are organised
deep.body: The picker sorts spec patterns into groups by what the texture does: sparkle and micro-metal, optical and interference, directional metal and brush, carbon and composite weave, clearcoat and coating, structure and geometry, surface and spray texture, weather and wear, machined hardware, and themed sets such as predator skins, voodoo, rising sun and let freedom ring. Definitive Spec Replacements is the largest group with 33; Source Pattern Plates has 24 and matches the plate finishes of the same name.

deep.heading: Choosing by job
deep.body: Want sparkle or flake: the Sparkle and Micro-Metal group. Want weave: Carbon and Composite Weave. Want brushed or machined: Directional Metal and Brush, Machined and Race Hardware. Want rainbow or oil film: Optical and Interference, or a holographic overlay over a pearl, metallic or chrome base. Want worn or weathered: Weather, Wear and Track plus a rougher base. Themed groups are loud, so lower strength before stacking another layer.

deep.heading: Every one changes shine only
deep.body: Each spec pattern lists which channels it touches by default (M, R or C) and you can tick or untick them. Roughness only is the safest choice for subtle texture.
